title: 2-CTA attention: a CTA pair shares a pair MMA, and each loads half of K/V

steps.title: Pair QKᵀ: cluster, pair TMEM, split K load, multicast commit (checks only S of the first K/V block)
Full 2-CTA pipeline: split V load, pair PV (TS), cross-CTA p_ready (release.cluster), causal
The cost of the cross-CTA handoff: p_ready switches to a release.cta remote arrive

cases.name: n1
cases.purpose: N=1: one cluster; only tile 0 of the leader has 1 valid row; the peer's Q and the last 64 keys of K are fully out of bounds (TMA fills zeros), and the peer still takes part in every pair MMA. O = V, LSE = scale·q·k.

cases.name: one_block
cases.purpose: N=128: only tile 0 of the leader is valid, and the peer's half of K (keys 64–127) is valid; B>1, H>1: 4-D tensor map coordinates and grid/cluster mapping.

cases.name: two_tiles
cases.purpose: N=256: leader tile 0 and peer tile 0 form exactly the first pair MMA (rows 0–255), two K/V blocks, D=128: the peer's row offset is +128.

cases.name: tile1_tail
cases.purpose: N=200: the peer's tile 0 has only 72 valid rows; the second K/V block has only 72 valid keys (keys 128–199), 64 of them in the leader's half of K and 8 in the peer's half.

cases.name: short_tail
cases.purpose: N=37, D=128: all 37 keys are in the leader's half of K; the peer's half is all TMA-filled zeros and must be masked.

cases.name: scale
cases.purpose: scale=1, logits in the hundreds: scale must come from p.scale; without subtracting the max the result overflows.

cases.name: uniform
cases.purpose: Q=0: O is the mean of V, LSE = ln N. Each of the two CTAs holds half of the V columns; missing one half gives a wrong result right away.

cases.name: ones_v
cases.purpose: V=1, 5 blocks, 2 clusters: the correction of O and the correction of ℓ must use the same α for O to equal 1; P of padding keys must be 0.

cases.name: position
cases.purpose: V[j]=j/N, 5 blocks: a wrong item index in the K/V ring buffer (K even, V odd) or a wrong parity reads another block; for D=64 a half of V is 32 columns with 64B swizzle.

cases.name: peaked
cases.purpose: D=128, 7 blocks, large logits: the max updates repeatedly, and the O correction in both CTAs must finish before the pair PV (p_ready collects all 512 arrives).

cases.name: peaked_d64
cases.purpose: D=64, FP16: N=513 is 1 more than a multiple of the block size; the second cluster has only 1 row (leader tile 0).

cases.name: ring
cases.purpose: 12 blocks, 24 ring items: the ring buffer wraps several times; each CTA waits on its own kv_empty, and a wrong parity reads a stale block or hangs.

cases.name: ring_d64
cases.purpose: D=64, 20 blocks, 40 ring items = 2.5 laps of a 16-stage ring: the D=64 stage count (16) and parity; the 64B swizzle of the V half must be right in every stage.

cases.name: medium
cases.purpose: Medium-size random data, D=128: 2 clusters, a full ping-pong over 8 blocks.

cases.name: medium_d64
cases.purpose: Medium-size random data, D=64, FP16.

cases.name: causal_n1
cases.purpose: Causal with N=1: the only query sees only itself.

cases.name: causal_pair
cases.purpose: Causal, N=256, large logits: block 2 of pair tile 0 is fully masked for the leader's rows (must not produce NaN), and the peer's diagonal block needs a mask.

cases.name: causal_tail
cases.purpose: Causal with N not a multiple of the block size: the diagonal mask and the tail mask apply at the same time.

cases.name: causal_position
cases.purpose: Causal, V[j]=j/N, D=128: a mask that is off by one reads values from future positions.

cases.name: causal_peaked
cases.purpose: Causal with large logits: masked elements in the diagonal block must not take part in the max; the second cluster has only 5 rows.

cases.name: causal_uniform
cases.purpose: Causal with Q=0: O[i] is the mean of V[0..i], LSE[i] = ln(i+1).

cases.name: causal_ones_v
cases.purpose: Causal with V=1: O must equal 1, including row 0, which has only one key.

cases.name: causal_medium
cases.purpose: Medium-size causal, D=128, 2 clusters: pair tile t walks only blocks 0..4c+2t+1 (c is the cluster index).

cases.name: causal_medium_d64
cases.purpose: Medium-size causal, D=64.

cases.name: peer_position
cases.purpose: Non-causal, D=128, N=190: the peer's tile 0 has only 62 rows; V[j]=j/N exposes the packing order of the peer's P (two adjacent keys swapped) and a wrongly loaded half of the V columns.

cases.name: peaked_fp16
cases.purpose: FP16, D=128, scale=1, large logits: the −127 clamp of the software exp2; the max jumps often in the first few blocks, and the two CTAs have different α.

cases.name: growing
cases.purpose: The max grows slowly per block, and the total is far above τ: conditional rescale must compare with the current reference (lab 41); the same holds for the peer's rows in the 2 clusters.

cases.name: growing_causal
cases.purpose: growing_max, causal, D=64: within one warp some rows need a correction and others do not (warp vote); the two CTAs of a pair tile vote separately.

cases.name: jump
cases.purpose: From key 650 the logits jump up: the jump block must move the reference and correct O, or P overflows to inf; the result must be right whichever half of K the jump block falls in.

cases.name: jump_causal
cases.purpose: jump_max, BF16, causal, D=128: within a tile some rows jump and some do not; the leader's and the peer's rows see the jump in different blocks.

cases.name: odd_tiles
cases.purpose: N=384 = 3 Q tiles: the leader's tile 1 (rows 256–383) is valid, and the peer's tile 1 is fully out of bounds; half of the pair MMA rows are padding.

cases.name: three_clusters
cases.purpose: N=1100: 3 clusters (an odd count); the last one has only 76 rows (leader tile 0); cluster index → q0 = 512·c.

cases.name: clusters_d128
cases.purpose: N=600, D=128: the second cluster has only 88 rows; for D=128 a half of V is 64 columns with 128B swizzle.

cases.name: causal_odd_tiles
cases.purpose: Causal, N=640: in the second cluster only the 128 rows of leader tile 0 are valid; the block count of pair tile 0 is set by N (5 blocks), not by the diagonal (6 blocks); tile 1 is fully out of bounds.

cases.name: causal_clusters
cases.purpose: Causal, 3 clusters, large logits: in each cluster tile 0 walks 2 fewer blocks than tile 1 (the last cluster is cut short by N).

cases.name: perf
cases.purpose: B·H=64, N=4096, D=128: 550 GFLOP, the same case as labs 22 and 34.

cases.name: perf_causal
cases.purpose: Same as above but causal: skipping blocks leaves about half the work.

cases.name: perf_d64
cases.purpose: D=64, FP16: the MMA per key is halved, so the exponentials (MUFU) take a larger share.

cases.name: perf_8k
cases.purpose: N=8192, D=128: 64 blocks per CTA; the main loop dominates, so the prologue/teardown matters least.
